bib.title: 5 Extracting domain-specific knowledge from unstructured data (Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, ch. 5)

question: How can unstructured domain text (the Rockefeller Archive Center diaries) be turned into entities and relations for a knowledge graph, using LLM prompting rather than traditional NLP pipelines?
contributions: Three iterations of an extraction prompt on one diary paragraph, with the failure at each step
Prompt engineering guidelines from the RAC project
Pros and cons of traditional NLP versus LLMs for KG building

limits: Prompts were tested on GPT-4o mini only; authors say newer models will differ and focus on principles.
Prompt evaluation is by eye on one paragraph; no precision, recall or F1 is reported. The chapter only recommends computing them per class.
The final prompt, JSON output format and fine-tuning run are not shown (point to the book's code repository).
Hallucination is named as the main LLM limitation and an open issue.
practices: Explore the data first; design for quirks such as full name then initial only (5.3.1).
Describe the task precisely and add dataset specifics such as abbreviations (5.3.3).
List the entity and relation classes of interest in the prompt and rename classes that underperform (5.3.3).
Give one complex, representative example containing every key relation type, with full clean names (5.3.3).
Use temperature 0 for fact extraction; if non-zero, rerun and measure output overlap (5.3.3).
Keep a unit-test list of snippets and expected outputs, run in bulk, inspect failures (5.3.3).
At each prompt milestone, build a mini-KG from a few dozen pages and eyeball it (5.3.3).
Evaluate with a QA manager marking correct/incorrect/missing, then per-class precision, recall, F1; an LLM judge is an alternative (5.3.3).
If no schema is known, run a generic extract-all prompt on a sample to get an explorative KG (5.3.3).
Do a couple of quick iterations then move to fine-tuning rather than endless prompt tuning (5.3.3).
Keep traditional NLP for security, massive datasets and streaming; LLM preannotation can bootstrap its training data (5.3.4).
Be consistent in relation direction across documents (5.2.2 note).
